themes.text: The economy is supportive (10 of 12 growth, jobs and credit gauges help stocks); the price of money is restrictive (7 of 11 rate, inflation and dollar/oil gauges hurt). Regime: overheating (growth up, inflation up); after such months the S&P's median next year was +9.8%, up 74% of the time. Across every macro condition tested, median next-year returns only ranged +7.3% to +13.9%, so macro sets the backdrop but has been a weak timing signal.
Real GDP 3.4% annualized last quarter, retail sales 6.8% y/y, factory output 2.1% y/y; consumer sentiment 48.0 is the lowest reading since 1952: people are spending while saying they feel worse.
Core PCE 3.1% and core CPI 2.6% against the Fed's 2% goal; headline CPI 3.7%; markets expect 2.28% a year over five years.
Fed funds 3.88% (+0.25 pts in 3 months); 2-year 4.69%, 10-year 4.99%, real 10-year 2.76% (higher than 99% of months since 2003). Curve 0.71 pts.
Unemployment 4.1% (0.0 pts in a year), payrolls 137k a month, weekly claims 202k; Sahm indicator 0.00 against a 0.5 trigger.
Baa corporate spread 1.52 pts (lower than 93% of months since 1986); financial conditions -0.47 (below 0 is looser than average); Fed balance sheet 2.9% y/y; M2 5.7% y/y.
Broad dollar 0.4% y/y; WTI averaged $93 this month.

meta.source: FRED (St. Louis Fed); S&P 500 from Yahoo Finance
meta.method: Fixed thresholds per indicator, written in advance. Regime months use data with a one-month publication lag.
